subject: RFI: Deployment patterns & GPU scaling — detailed sizing workbook attached
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@nimbusai.com, alex@NimbusAI.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Deployment patterns & GPU scaling — detailed sizing workbook attached

Alex / Nimbus team,

Thanks for the RFP follow-up call yesterday. Attached is our detailed sizing workbook that maps your target workloads to recommended reservation slots, GPU families, and throughput projections. Highlights in this message to make it easier to scan: 

- Assumptions we used (see Workbook tab: "Assumptions"):
  - Peak concurrent inference pipelines: 12 (interactive chat) + 6 (batch reranker) + 4 (embedding bulk jobs)
  - Model mix: 60% Llama2-70B (int8 q4), 30% open-encoder-13B (fp16), 10% custom-re-ranker (fp16)
  - Target p95 latency (interactive): 200 ms; p50 for batch: 400 ms
  - Average sequence length: 384 tokens (interactive), 1,200 tokens (batch embedding flows)

- Recommended GPU families and slotting (Workbook tab: "GPU_Recommendations"):
  - H100-80GB (dense/high-TPS interactive): 6 slots — preferred for low tail latency at scale
  - A100-40GB (cost/perf balanced): 8 slots — good for mixed fp16 and quantized int8 models
  - L4x (inference-efficient edge/low-cost): 4 slots — for embeddings and predictable batch workloads

- Reservation plan (Workbook tab: "Reserve_Plan"):
  - Committed pool: 10 slots (H100/A100 blend) provisioned in us-west; planned burst policy to scale +6 slots in us-east for failover traffic
  - Burst capacity: 30% of committed pool available on demand (policy: 1.5x sustained for 15 min, 2x for 2 min short bursts)

- Throughput modeling (Workbook tab: "Throughput_Model"):
  - Interactive (Llama2-70B int8): 18 reqs/s per H100 slot at 384 tokens avg (with KV cache reuse); target 95th tail within 200 ms when concurrency per-slot <= 8
  - Batch embedding (open-encoder-13B): 140 embed/sec per A100-40 slot with batching window 100ms; optimize with prefix caching for repeated prefixes

I've also included a short appendix (pdf) explaining kernel-selection behavior, quantization tradeoffs, and guidance on enabling prefix/kv caching safely for stateful chat flows. If you want, we can convert the workbook into a live spreadsheet during next week's workshop and run a few sensitivity scenarios together (GPU pricing +/-10%, model mix shifts, and 2x traffic growth).

Next steps (suggested):
1) Confirm target p95 SLOs and regional mix (us-west vs us-east).
2) We run two quick scenario runs and return an updated workbook by EOD Thu.
3) If acceptable, we draft commitment tiers and an initial proposal for dedicated capacity.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), gpu-mix-profiles-2026.pdf (whitepaper)

Best,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex@NimbusAI.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Deployment patterns & GPU scaling — detailed sizing workbook attached

Ben — thanks for the workbook, this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs after a quick pass: 

1) You call out H100-80 as the low-tail option — can you quantify the p99 tail improvement vs A100-40 for the chat workload at ~10k daily active users?
2) For the burst policy, how does Redwood guarantee that burst capacity is available during concurrent region failover (us-west outage)? Is that part of the SLA or an operational best-effort?
3) We have an internal preference to avoid more than two GPU families in a single committed pool. Can you show a 2-family plan with comparable latency and cost?

Also, our procurement team will need a short note about on-prem options and any additional compliance fees (SOC2 + HIPAA onboarding). I've cc'd procurement@nimbusai.com.

Thanks — can you respond by EOD Wed?

— Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@NimbusAI.com>, procurement@nimbusai.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Deployment patterns & GPU scaling — detailed sizing workbook attached

Alex — quick answers below, then I attached a short 2-family alternative in the same workbook (tab: "2_Family_Option").

1) p99 tail: based on our internal benchmarks using the same model and seq length, H100-80 shows ~35-45% p99 tail reduction vs A100-40 at equivalent throughput due to larger on-device memory (fewer KV cache evictions) and improved attention kernel throughput. Workbook includes p50/p95/p99 comparisons per-slot under synthetic traffic.

2) Burst availability for region failover: we offer two mechanisms — managed burst (Redwood-managed spare capacity across regions) and reserved cross-region contingency (a subset of committed slots kept in a geographically separate pool). Managed burst is covered by our runbook and has an availability SLA tie-in at the enterprise tier; reserved cross-region contingency is included as part of Dedicated plus a minimal cross-region reserve fee. I'll include suggested language for both in the pricing appendix.

3) Two-family plan: we modeled H100 + A100 only (no L4x). Outcome: marginal p95 degradation (~5–10ms for chat workloads) with ~4–7% cost increase vs the three-family mix, but you get simpler operations and fewer images/kernels to manage. See tab "2_Family_Option" for the full cost/latency tradeoff table.

Procurement note (short):
- On-prem offering: available as a Private deployment; additional integration and packaging fee applies. Standard SOC2 attestation included for Dedicated; HIPAA onboarding incurs professional services time (estimate 2–4 weeks) and a one-time compliance onboarding fee. Detailed terms are in the pricing appendix.

I pushed an updated workbook (same filenames) to the shared link. If that works, I'll schedule a 30-min run-through with engineering to walk the sensitivity scenarios.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that addresses most of our questions. Two final asks before we loop legal: 

- Can you provide a 48-hour failover test plan (what Redwood will simulate, what Nimbus needs to verify, success criteria)?
- Please include expected unit pricing ranges for the three commitment tiers (bronze/silver/gold) in the workbook; procurement prefers ranges rather than fixed numbers right now.

If you can drop those by EOD Mon, we can put this into our internal procurement review and share heads-up to legal.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Alex
